metaTitle: Free Contractor Invoice Template - Construction & Trades
metaDescription: Free contractor invoice template for construction, trade pros, and subcontractors. Itemize labor, materials, and milestones with zero watermarks.
intro: Generate professional contractor invoices itemizing labor hours, materials, and project milestones in seconds with zero watermarks.

howTo.title: How to Create a Contractor Invoice
howTo.subtitle: Clear, dispute-proof contractor invoices in three simple steps.

steps.title: Enter Contractor and Jobsite Details
steps.description: Add your trade business name, state licence number, client billing address, and the physical jobsite address where work took place.
steps.tip: Always record the jobsite address separately from the client's office address.

steps.title: Itemize Labor, Supplies, and Permits
steps.description: Separate skilled labor hours from materials, building fixtures, and permit fees for complete billing transparency.
steps.tip: Include the client's work order or purchase order (PO) number to avoid billing delays.

steps.title: Download the PDF or Print on the Jobsite
steps.description: Generate an instant vector PDF to email from your phone or print a hard copy directly for on-site sign-off.
steps.tip: State payment milestones clearly (for example: 50% deposit, 50% on final inspection).

whatItMustContain.title: What a Contractor Invoice Must Contain
whatItMustContain.subtitle: Key elements needed for construction, electrical, plumbing, and trade contracting compliance.
whatItMustContain.disclaimer: General information, not legal or tax advice. Check your local rules.

items.title: Contractor Identity and Licence
items.description: Your registered business name, contact details, and state or municipal contractor licence number [Verify with official source: state contractor licensing regulations].

items.title: Client and Jobsite Physical Address
items.description: The client's billing information plus the exact physical address where the construction or trade work was performed.

items.title: Contract or PO Reference Number
items.description: The original estimate number, client purchase order, or change-order identifier for clear cross-referencing.

items.title: Separated Labor and Materials
items.description: An itemized breakdown distinguishing hourly labor from raw building materials, fixtures, and equipment rentals.

items.title: Deposits and Milestone Credits
items.description: Clear accounting of deposits already received, progress draws, and any agreed retainage holdback amount.

items.title: Payment Terms and Remittance Details
items.description: Direct bank transfer details (ACH or wire), check mailing instructions, and due dates [Verify with official source: statutory mechanics lien notice deadlines].

faq.title: Contractor Invoicing FAQs
faq.subtitle: Answers to common questions about trade billing, materials tax, and milestone payments.

items.question: Why should contractors separate labor and materials on invoices?
items.answer: Separating labor and materials provides full transparency to the client and simplifies sales tax reporting. In many jurisdictions, sales tax applies to physical building materials but not to labor [Verify with official source: state sales tax rules on contractor labor].

items.question: Can I record milestone deposits or retainage?
items.answer: Yes. Add an item with a negative amount or use the discount field to record previous deposits, showing the exact remaining balance due.

items.question: Can I generate contractor invoices on my phone at the jobsite?
items.answer: Yes. The editor switches to a touch-friendly card view on mobile screens, letting you create and download clean PDF invoices right from your truck or jobsite.

items.question: What happens if a client disputes a contractor invoice?
items.answer: Having itemized work orders, jobsite addresses, and written change orders on your invoice provides the legal documentation needed to resolve disputes quickly.
